newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA ION, MANNESMANN UNIT IN JV.
newsitem.headline: INDIA ION, MANNESMANN UNIT IN JV.

text.p: Indian water treatment firm Ion Exchange (India) Ltd said it is forming a joint venture with Mannesmann Demag to market energy generation and pollution control solutions through waste water treatment.
The two firms will equally own the capital of the new venture, Ion Exchange said on Monday.
"The thrust areas of the new company will be the Indian subcontinent and South-east Asia, the Gulf region and East and South Africa," the company said in a statement.
Mannesmann Demag's subsidiary Mannesmann Seiffert GmbH will provide technology to the joint venture.
"We will undertake turnkey contracts in India, South-East Asia and the Gulf region," a company spokesman said.
"The conservative sales projections we have made indicate show sales turnover touching 2.5 billion rupees ($70 million) in three years."
There is no capital cost as the joint venture is not building a factory. The fabrication will be subcontracted to third parties.
India is a good base because of lower cost of manpower and fabrication, the spokesman said.
